name: Partial Equivalence Queries Complexity
definition: The **Partial Equivalence Queries Complexity** of $\mathcal{H}$ is the minimum worst-case number of partial equivalence queries needed to identify an unknown target in $\mathcal{H}$, where a query is a partial Boolean function and a negative reply supplies a point on which it disagrees with the target.
graph_summary: Minimum worst-case number of partial equivalence queries needed to identify the target.
origin_references: The partial-equivalence-query learning model is introduced in \cite{maass1992lower}.

monotonic.proof: A partial-equivalence-query strategy that identifies every target in $\mathcal H$ remains a valid strategy for every target in a subfamily $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H$, with no additional queries.

c_monotonic.proof: Simulate a learner for the original class, extending each fibre hypothesis with the fixed labels.  Partial-equivalence answers restrict back to valid answers on the fibre.
